newsitem.title: USA: Trend-Lines sees fy 97 sales up 15-20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Trend-Lines sees fy 97 sales up 15-20 pct.

text.p: Trend-Lines Inc said on Wednesday that it expects sales to increase 15-20 percent, or $240 to $250 million, in fiscal 1997 compared to fiscal 1996 in part because of a planned expansion of its retail stores.
In an announcement accompanying its fourth quarter earnings report, Trend-Lines said it planned to open 40 to 50 new stores in fiscal 1997 and expected sales to increase accordingly.
The company reported that it had opened 26 new stores during fiscal 1996.

"Estimated sales growth is dependent upon a stable retail climate, sales per catalog comparable with last year's results and the company's estimated timing for opening new retail stores," the company said in a statement.

"The company also expects that its gross margin should be approximately 32 percent to 33 percent in fiscal 1997," it said. It attributed the prediction to the plans to expand its retail stores, which historically have had lower gross margins than its catalog business.
"Retail sales should represent a greater proportion of sales in fiscal 1997," the company said.
Trend-Lines on Wednesday reported fourth-quarter net of $0.20 a share, or $2.2 million, up from a loss of $0.51 a share, or $5.6 million in the same period a year earlier.
